# You're inside a real Advisor Prep Hero workspace

This is running in your browser. No install, no account, nothing saved to a server. It's a pretend consulting engagement, pre-loaded so you can poke around instead of staring at an empty screen.

Everything here is a real Advisor Prep Hero surface. The files are real files. The editor is the real editor. The AI sidebar talks to a real model.

## What to try

1. Open `Meridian Growth Partners/Engagement Summary.md` to see how a consultant organizes the opening phase of an engagement inside Advisor Prep Hero.
2. Open `Meridian Growth Partners/Discovery Notes.md` to see interview notes structured for AI synthesis.
3. Open `Meridian Growth Partners/Discovery Synthesis.aichat` to watch a saved AI conversation where the consultant asks the AI to pull common themes from three interviews.
4. Open the AI sidebar and ask it something about the open file.

On your own machine, these files live in a folder you pick, and your API key goes straight from your computer to the model. Client strategy, interview transcripts, and competitive intelligence never route through a server you do not control. That's the reason a consultant operating under an NDA can use Advisor Prep Hero on live engagement work.

Refresh the page and the workspace comes back to where it started.

# Engagement Summary: Meridian Growth Partners

**Client:** Meridian Growth Partners (holding company)
**Operating entity:** Meridian Precision Components, Inc. (a Meridian portfolio company)
**Engagement type:** Operational improvement, go-to-market strategy
**Engagement start:** May 19, 2026
**Lead consultant:** [Your name]
**Sponsor:** Andrea Stanton, CEO, Meridian Precision Components
**PE sponsor contact:** Thomas Ruiz, Operating Partner, Meridian Growth Partners

## Background

Meridian Precision Components manufactures custom metal fittings and assemblies for HVAC, plumbing, and light industrial OEM customers. Roughly 60% of revenue comes from three legacy OEM relationships dating to 2011 to 2016, all of which are on annual contracts with thin margins. The PE sponsor acquired the business in 2023 with a 5-year hold thesis centered on revenue diversification and EBITDA margin expansion. Current EBITDA margin is approximately 11%; the sponsor's model requires 17% to 18% by exit.

## Engagement objective

Assess the operational and commercial levers available to move EBITDA margin from 11% to 17% within 36 months, and recommend a sequenced improvement roadmap the management team can execute without adding significant corporate overhead.

## Preliminary hypotheses (to be tested in discovery)

1. **Pricing:** Legacy OEM contracts are below market and have not been renegotiated in three or more years. A structured repricing program may recover 200 to 350 basis points of margin without volume loss.
2. **Customer mix:** The business is concentrated in three accounts. Reducing concentration and adding higher-margin industrial distribution customers diversifies risk and likely improves blended margin.
3. **Production throughput:** Anecdotal evidence from the plant tour suggests the scheduling process creates idle time between runs. A lean scheduling review may unlock capacity without capital expenditure.
4. **SG&A:** The business added headcount in 2024 that has not yet translated into revenue growth. An SG&A rationalization may be warranted, though this needs careful handling given the management team's tenure.

## Discovery plan

- **Week 1 (May 19 to 23):** CEO, CFO, and VP Operations interviews. Plant tour. Initial data request fulfilled.
- **Week 2 (May 26 to 30):** Sales and customer service interviews. Customer contract review. Preliminary financial analysis.
- **Week 3 (June 2 to 6):** Synthesis and hypothesis refinement. Draft findings deck outline.
- **Week 4 (June 9 to 12):** Findings presentation to PE sponsor and management team.

## Files in this workspace

- `Discovery Notes.md` - Interview notes, organized by session
- `Discovery Synthesis.aichat` - AI-assisted synthesis of interview themes
- `Engagement Summary.md` - This file

# Discovery Notes: Meridian Growth Partners

Rough notes from discovery interviews. These are working notes, not transcripts. Kept inside Advisor Prep Hero to work with the AI; the polished findings go into the deck.

---

## Interview 1: Andrea Stanton, CEO
**Date:** May 20, 2026 | **Duration:** 75 min

**On the legacy OEM relationships:**
Andrea confirmed all three anchor accounts are on contracts that were last repriced in 2021 or earlier. She said the team has been "afraid to push" on price because the volume feels irreplaceable. Her words: "If we lose one of them, we lose 20% of the business overnight." She acknowledged this fear has probably kept them from testing what the market will bear.

**On the sales organization:**
Two-person inside sales team plus Andrea herself carrying two of the three anchor accounts personally. No dedicated outbound function. New customer acquisition has been almost entirely inbound referral for the past four years. Andrea said, "We've never really had to sell. The phone rang and we answered it." She seems aware this is a problem but hasn't had bandwidth to address it.

**On operations:**
Praises the plant team highly. Said VP Operations Marcus Webb has been there 14 years and knows the floor "better than anyone." Some frustration that scheduling decisions still flow through Marcus personally and create bottlenecks when he travels. No comment on throughput data; deferred to Marcus.

**Tone:** Open and self-aware. Not defensive. She knows the business is at an inflection point and seems genuinely interested in the engagement.

---

## Interview 2: David Park, CFO
**Date:** May 21, 2026 | **Duration:** 60 min

**On financial data:**
David pulled the P&L by customer for the past three years. Confirmed the three legacy accounts are averaging 9.8% gross margin. The four smaller customers they added in 2024 and 2025 are averaging 18.4% gross margin. He noted this without prompting; he clearly already knows the concentration story.

**On the 2024 headcount addition:**
Added a customer service coordinator and an inside sales coordinator in Q3 2024. Revenue in the accounts they were supposed to support has been flat. David was careful but it was clear he thinks these hires have not paid off. He said, "We might have added capacity before we figured out what to do with it."

**On capex:**
Last meaningful equipment investment was 2019. Two of the five CNC lines are running at capacity during peak weeks. He thinks there is a capex conversation coming in the next 12 to 18 months regardless of what we recommend.

**Tone:** Measured, analytical, slightly guarded. Comfortable with numbers, less comfortable with soft topics like personnel.

---

## Interview 3: Marcus Webb, VP Operations
**Date:** May 22, 2026 | **Duration:** 90 min + plant floor walk

**On scheduling:**
Marcus runs the production schedule from a whiteboard and a spreadsheet. He does the daily scheduling himself every morning before the floor opens. He said, "I know where every hour of capacity is." When I asked what happens when he is out, he paused and said, "We manage." The team clearly depends on his knowledge in a way that is a single point of failure.

**On throughput:**
Marcus showed me their run log. Average changeover between part families is 47 minutes. He believes this is unavoidable given the customization level. I am not sure that is true; need to compare against SMED benchmarks for similar operations. Three idle-time events of more than two hours in the past 30 days, all attributable to a late material delivery from one supplier.

**On the customer mix:**
Marcus does not think about customers in margin terms. His frame is volume and complexity. He prefers the legacy OEM accounts because they run high volume, low complexity. The newer accounts run lower volume, higher complexity setups. He said, "The new customers are harder to run."

**Tone:** Confident, territorial about his domain, genuinely knowledgeable. He sees operational complexity from the customer mix shift as a real cost, and he is probably right; this needs to be quantified.

# About this demo

This is the in-browser version of Advisor Prep Hero, pre-loaded with a fictional consulting engagement so you have something real to look at.

The client, the names, and the situations are all made up for illustration. Nothing here is consulting advice, and the AI's job in the real app is to help you produce a first synthesis or draft you review, not to replace your judgment.

What's different from the real app: this demo uses a shared, rate-limited key so you can try the AI without setting anything up. On your own machine you bring your own key (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, or a local model through Ollama). Your files and your key never leave your computer. Client interview notes and strategy work never touch a server you do not control.

When you're ready, download the 30-day trial at advisorprephero.com.
